data.title: Cruise ship suspends global voyage due to fuel costs
data.description:
A resident of the ship said that changes to the itinerary, unreliable Internet access and declining food quality had already pushed many to leave the ship in the past few months

A US cruise ship on an around-the-world voyage that touted its cabins as floating homes suspended its three-year journey in Cambodia due to fuel costs, forcing hundreds of passengers to disembark.

The MV Odyssey set sail two years ago on a voyage to the seven continents marketed as combining long-term living at sea with global travel. Its operator had offered to “make the Odyssey your permanent home,” with the purchase price of a suite for the lifetime of the vessel starting at about US$230,000.

For now, it is docked at the Cambodian port of Sihanoukville on the Gulf of Thailand, with no certain departure date.

The ship has been carrying 203 passengers, mostly Americans, along with 156 crew members, according to Cambodian officials.

It has a 650-passenger capacity.

Its Florida-based operator, Villa Vie Residences, said monthly fuel expenses per cabin that historically averaged US$1,800 have reached an estimated US$6,000 to US$8,000 in parts of Asia due to the war in Iran.

The company said it sought to reduce fuel consumption by slowing the itinerary and spending more time in port, but was unable to offset the surging costs.

Traffic has been curtailed in the Strait of Hormuz since the war in Iran began, squeezing supplies of all kinds of petroleum-based fuels, especially in Southeast Asia, and sharply increasing prices.

“We have been unable to continue carrying the resulting operating losses,” Villa Vie Residences said in a statement on Tuesday. “Passing the full increase on to residents is not a realistic solution. Our focus now is on supporting residents, crew, and employees” while it tries to restructure.

“The company is working with residents to coordinate disembarkation and identify temporary living arrangements,” it said.

However, some passengers said they received no support and had to make their own arrangements after being given seven hours notice on Tuesday to disembark. Some were devastated and expressed hope a new company could rescue the venture so life at sea can continue.

Paul and Lynn Montoya, a retired couple from Wyoming, said they bought a window cabin and had expected to sail for years. They boarded the ship 17 months ago in Panama.

Paul praised the concept of residential cruising, but said the shipowner lacked the expertise to make the business financially sustainable.

While rising fuel costs had been cited publicly as the reason for the suspension, he said the company had already been struggling.

Changes to the itinerary, unreliable Internet access and declining food quality had pushed many residents to leave the ship in the past few months, he said.

Lynn said that residents were repeatedly asked to contribute additional money for fuel and other expenses, including a fresh call to raise funds for fuel to get out of Cambodia.

She said the crew members were also not paid.

“We were tired of every two to four weeks being asked for money for fuel, money for everything,” she said.

“We had hopes, but they just kept sinking further and further into the hole through mismanagement,” she added.

The company could not immediately be contacted for comment.

Yet for some, even the financial and logistical turmoil could not outweigh the extraordinary experience of traveling the world and living at sea.

Carol Larson, 69, and her sister Crystal Lavering, 72, occupied separate cabins aboard the ship for 18 months. The siblings, from California, described the suspension as heartbreaking, and hoped the cruise would be resuscitated.

“I hope there is a movement for the residents to buy the ship and I am hoping that goes through because it’s a dream to live on the ship and I don’t want it to end,” Larson said.

Lavering said her health improved during her time on the ship and that she did not need to use a cane to walk anymore.

“You come to this ship to live ... it’s just sad that it’s all over,” she said.

Larson bought her cabin for US$120,000, paid in installments, in addition to monthly maintenance fees, under a plan that had promised the possibility of living aboard for up to 15 years.

She blamed US President Donald Trump for the ship’s woes as fuel costs spiked due to the Iran war, in addition to poor management.

However, she said she did not regret her investment.

“Because it was a start-up company, I believe that it was a risk. From the very first day, I said to myself that if it lasts a year, I can walk away and feel like I got my money’s worth... I still feel that way. I feel blessed to have been part of the experiment of residential cruising,” she said.

The ship arrived in Sihanoukville on Oct. 23 and was scheduled to depart on Wednesday, according to a statement from Long Dimanche, the deputy governor of Preah Sihanouk.

The ship’s operator has not yet publicly confirmed any date of departure.

Built in 1993 and operated under different names by several cruise lines before being becalmed by the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, the Odyssey was bought by Villa Vie Residences in 2023.

Its current cruise, originally intended to last three-and-a-half years, began in October 2024 in Belfast, where the ship had been refitted. A second cruise had been tentatively scheduled to end in August 2030.

The Odyssey is not the first cruise ship Sihanoukville has hosted in crisis.

In February 2020, the MS Westerdam was allowed to dock in Cambodia after being turned away at five ports in other nations because of fears of COVID-19, which just a month earlier had started to spread from China.

It carried 1,455 passengers, more than 600 of them US citizens.

After being stranded at sea for two weeks, then-Cambodian prime minister Hun Sen allowed it to dock for what he said were humanitarian reasons.

Cambodia won plaudits as passengers were welcomed ashore and arrangements were made for them to fly home.

data.title: Sri Lanka’s Tamil farmers fight to reclaim land after civil war
data.description:
Tired but resolute, dozens of Tamil cattle farmers have held a round-the-clock vigil for almost three years in eastern Sri Lanka, protesting what they call land “theft.”

At shift change, farmers exchange news before settling beneath a tarpaulin beside photographs of the bloodied bodies of their dead cows.

“They have been shooting our cattle, threatening us, assaulting us and spraying pesticides or poison on the pasture lands where our cattle graze,” said Seenithamby Thiyagarajah, president of the local farmers’ association, detailing the push his community felt from recipients of a state-funded program that was driving them off their land.

“Over 5,700 cows have been destroyed like this. Even after complaining numerous times to the police and all relevant places, we received no resolution,” he said.

The alleged perpetrators are farmers who have benefited from the state-funded Mahaweli development scheme. Most are Sinhalese, the country’s majority ethnic group, settling on land claimed by the largely Hindu Tamil minority, which makes up about 12 percent of the population.

The government denied any forcible attempts to remove people from their land.

Sri Lanka’s 1983 to 2009 civil war between government forces and Tamil separatists killed more than 100,000 people, according to UN data.

Nearly two decades later, land disputes continue to fuel ethnic grievances.

Thiyagarajah said that settlers aided by the scheme have encroached on grazing land used by the roughly 1,000 cattle farmers he represents.

Courts have repeatedly ordered the eviction of the scheme-backed settler farmers, he said.

“Things are peaceful, for a while, but then the illegal cultivators entered again, ruining our land and destroying our cattle,” he said.

Other communities are also fighting to reclaim land.

Ambalavar Nallathambi Velayutham, 64, an indigenous community leader, wants his rice fields back.

Armed with renewed land deeds renewed with local authorities, Velayutham and neighbors in Kunjankulam returned to farming fields they had abandoned during the war.

Sri Lankan Forest Department officials told them the land was a reserve, Velayutham said.

“We said: ‘This land belonged to our ancestors.’ They replied: ‘That won’t do. You must leave,’” he added.

Fearing reprisals, most villagers abandoned their efforts.

One night, a villager spotted forestry officials’ mobile phones glowing in the darkness.

“They dug there and planted boundary stones,” Velayutham said, pointing to the markers.

Repeated appeals to local authorities, the prime minister and president have brought no result, he said.

“This land has neither been freed nor handed back to us,” he said. “If they release this farmland and we get it back from the Forest Department, I believe this will provide a great opportunity.”

Land disputes have multiplied across Sri Lanka’s Eastern Province, where Tamils are a major ethnic group.

Examples include an army barracks encroaching on a school, while government departments responsible for archeology, wildlife or forests claim farmland, temples and private property.

Officials designate land cultivated by Tamils as forest or wildlife reserves, “obstructing development or agricultural activities for them,” said Sabarathinam Sivayoganathan, 57, president of the Eastern Province Civil Society Activists Union.

The scale of these occupations is unclear, with no public statistics and residents risking intimidation by asking questions, he said.

Opposition Member of Parliament Rasamanickam R. Shanakiyan said that population figures point to a deliberate effort to change the region’s demographics.

“In the Eastern Province, the Sinhala population has increased by 700 percent since independence in 1948,” he said, compared with 200 percent nationally.

“This has happened through state-sponsored colonization,” he said, accusing the government of altering the ethnic balance of the north and east through land settlements.

Sri Lankan President Anura Kumara Dissanayake’s election in 2024 has brought little change, Shanakiyan said, despite campaign promises to the contrary.

He accused the government of failing to honor commitments in the lead up to the election that it would release land, protect minority rights and deliver wider political reforms.

“On these promises, nothing’s been delivered,” he said. “You feel a growing sense of frustration, maybe anger in the population.”

Land ownership disputes continue to fuel tensions, resentment and accusations online and on the ground between Sinhalese and Tamils across eastern Sri Lanka.

The Sri Lankan government said it has commissioned a report on changes to land records since the civil war and whether they should be corrected.

“We will never forcibly acquire people’s land,” Sri Lankan Minister of Environment Dhammika Patabendi told reporters in an e-mail.

“Based on the recommendations of this report, we believe that these issues can be resolved promptly and fairly,” he said.

However, as torrential rain drums on the tarpaulin sheltering the angry farmers, Thiyagarajah remains unconvinced.

“For 1,010 days, alongside this road and under this tent, we have been taking part day and night. Justice has still not been granted to our people,” he said. “Today, our people live in constant fear that today or tomorrow our cattle will be destroyed.”

data.title: Local shares fall by almost 2.5 percent
data.description:
TECH LOSSES: ‘Tech stocks had gained substantially since the beginning of this year,’ so the disappointing earnings prompted investors to trim holdings, an analyst said

Shares in Taiwan plunged by just under 2.5 percent yesterday, led by major artificial intelligence (AI)-related stocks, after tech stocks on US markets saw heavy losses overnight amid growing concerns that massive AI investments would not deliver comparable returns, analysts said.

The TAIEX closed down 1,156.50 points, or 2.49 percent, at 45,211.83 on turnover of NT$877.730 billion (US$27.03 billion).

“After the latest earnings reports by major American cloud service providers, worries over AI spending came back to haunt investor sentiment,” Concord Capital Management Corp (康和投顧) analyst Lu Chin-wei (呂晉維) said.

Alphabet’s disappointing sales renewed AI concerns, sending its shares plunging overnight, while Amazon.com shares also slumped on its soaring AI spending.

“Tech stocks had gained substantially since the beginning of this year, so such disappointing earnings reports simply prompted investors to trim their holdings and pocket gains,” Lu said.

After the tech-heavy NASDAQ fell 1.38 percent on Thursday, the electronics index in Taiwan fell 2.90 percent yesterday.

Contract chipmaker Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (台積電), which accounts for more than 40 percent of total market value, lost 1.86 percent to close at NT$2,370, contributing about 360 points to the TAIEX’s decline.

Among other semiconductor stocks, smartphone integrated circuit designer MediaTek Inc (聯發科) shed 3.21 percent to close at NT$3,915, while IC packaging and testing firm ASE Technology Holding Co (日月光投控) closed down 2.20 percent at NT$668.

Application-specific IC designer Alchip Technologies (世芯) shed 6.93 percent to close at NT$3,425.

Elsewhere in the tech sector, iPhone assembler and AI server maker Hon Hai Precision Industry Co (鴻海精密) slid 1.01 percent to close at NT$245.50, while Quanta Computer Inc (廣達), another AI server supplier, was unchanged at NT$318.

Investors rushed to park their money in select safe havens, with Chunghwa Telecom Co (中華電信) up 1.27 percent to close at NT$160 and Far EasTone Telecommunications Co (遠傳電信) closing 0.88 percent higher at NT$114.

“The financial sector also appeared resilient. I suspect government-led funds stood on the buy side,” Lu said.

The financial index dropped 0.16 percent, with CTBC Financial Holding Co (中信金控) closing up 0.66 percent at NT$75.80, E. Sun Financial Holding Co (玉山金控) up 0.10 percent at NT$49.05 and Fubon Financial Holding Co (富邦金控) falling 0.31 percent to NT$161.50.

Among safe havens in the old-economy sector, food brand Uni-President Enterprises Corp (統一企業) closed up 1.52 percent at NT$80.20 and Wei Chuan Foods Corp (味全食品) rose 9.72 percent to NT$13.55.

“Turnover shrank further, indicating many investors were reluctant to buy on the dip as they feared uncertainty ahead of the mid-term elections in the United States,” Lu said. “As the TAIEX fell below the technical resistance ahead of 45,300 points, the 120-day moving average, more losses are possible.”

Foreign institutional investors sold a net NT$112.47 billion on the market yesterday, Taiwan Stock Exchange data showed.

data.title: MediaTek gains new AI customer
data.description:
‘ON SCHEDULE’: Chief executive officer Rick Tsai said that TSMC ‘remains our most important partner’ as MediaTek seeks to meet robust customer demand

Chip designer MediaTek Inc (聯發科) yesterday said it has secured a second customer for its customized artificial intelligence (AI) accelerator for data centers, while volume production of a second-generation chip for an existing customer is on track for early 2028, potentially easing market concerns about possible delays.

This is a new customer and, crucially, not from China, MediaTek said.

The remarks were meant to dismiss speculation that ByteDance Ltd (字節跳動), the parent company of TikTok, was the second customer for MediaTek’s new customized AI application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) business.

“It is on track, on schedule. We understand there is some noise about the tape-out schedule,” MediaTek chief executive officer Rick Tsai (蔡力行) told investors during an earnings call.

The company’s second AI chip is a powerful XPU using multi-die architecture, he said.

A few dies have already been taped out, while another, larger and more complex die is on schedule to tape out in the coming weeks, he said.

Overall, MediaTek expects to ramp up volume production of the AI accelerator in the first quarter of 2028, he said.

Addressing investor concerns over the adoption of Intel Corp’s advanced packaging technology, called EMIB-T, Tsai said that Intel’s packaging process is “our absolute priority.”

“We are working very closely with our IDM [integrated device manufacturer] partner, with a primary focus on yield improvements,” he said.

MediaTek is using Intel’s EMIB-T advanced packaging for the second-generation project, while continuing to work with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC, 台積電).

However, MediaTek is not dependent on a single supplier, Tsai said.

“It is critical to make clear that TSMC remains our most important partner,” he said, adding that the company must adapt to changing customer requirements amid a rapidly growing AI market.

MediaTek said that its first AI ASIC program is progressing smoothly, with initial shipments commencing last month.

The chip is projected to generate US$2.5 billion in revenue this quarter, it said.

MediaTek said it anticipates revenue from the program next year to be at the high end of its target at about US$16 billion, capturing roughly 20 percent of the total AI ASIC market.

“This confidence is underpinned by our solid supply outlook. We are working closely with our supply chain partners for additional capacity to meet the strong customer demand,” Tsai said.

MediaTek has not named its existing customer, widely reported to be Google, with MediaTek designing a tensor processing unit — an AI ASIC — for it.

MediaTek said that it is working with its customer on a third-generation AI ASIC project and is in discussions to finalize the details.

The chip designer yesterday said it expects robust revenue growth this quarter of 25 to 32 percent sequentially to between NT$210.1 billion and NT$221.8 billion (US$6.47 billion and US$6.83 billion).

On an annual basis, that would be growth of 40 to 48 percent, it said.

Based on the revenue guidance for this quarter, MediaTek expects full-year revenue growth in US dollar terms would exceed its previous target of high-single-digit percentage growth.

Gross margin is expected to be 43.5 to 46.5 percent this quarter, compared with 46.3 percent last quarter, MediaTek said.

Operating profit margin from this quarter through next year is expected to show a marked improvement, it said.

The firm expects operating margin of at least 20 percent next year, as production of AI ASIC scales, MediaTek chief financial officer David Ku (顧大為) told investors.

Net profit last quarter expanded 14.6 percent sequentially to NT$28.2 billion from NT$24.61 billion in the second quarter, MediaTek said.

That represented annual growth of 10.8 percent from NT$25.45 billion.

Earnings per share rose to NT$17.5 last quarter from NT$15.28 in the second quarter and NT$15.84 in the third quarter last year.

data.title: Hon Hai expects revenue growth in double digits
data.description:
Manufacturing giant Hon Hai Precision Industry Co (鴻海精密) yesterday said it expects revenue to grow by a double-digit percentage next year, driven by robust demand for artificial intelligence (AI) data center-related products.

“We are likely to see a K-shaped divergence next year, with AI data center-related business continuing to grow, while other businesses would follow a different trajectory,” Hon Hai chairman Young Liu (劉揚偉) said on the sidelines of the Hon Hai Technology Day conference in Taipei.

Hon Hai’s revenue last year rose 18.13 percent year-on-year to about NT$8.1 trillion (US$249.4 billion), company data showed.

Recent concerns over an AI industry bubble might be overstated, as market demand remains clear, Liu said, adding that concern about financial risks at major AI companies was an overly negative view.

Supply-chain demand far exceeds capacity, making the situation difficult to describe simply as a “shortage,” he said.

Liu met with OpenAI chief executive officer Sam Altman.

The two discussed potential cooperation.

Liu declined to disclose details.

As AI data center demand continues to grow, Hon Hai plans to add more capacity to its six factory buildings in Houston, Texas, Liu said.

Hon Hai is not moving away from China, Liu said, adding that it remains a major market for its customers.

Regarding a proposed Taiwanese industrial park in Texas, with an investment of up to US$4 billion, Liu said that as the local AI manufacturing supply chain is incomplete, Taiwanese suppliers of key components have to build capacity there.

Hon Hai hopes the project could develop into what Liu described as a “third-generation science park,” following Hsinchu as the first generation and Tainan as the second.

Such a park should go beyond hosting individual manufacturers or assembly sites and instead form a complete industrial ecosystem, supported by suppliers of molds, forming and processing services, cables, connectors and printed circuit boards, Liu said.

The company yesterday showcased an Nvidia Corp DSX POD, a modular data center developed with Teco Electric & Machinery Co (東元電機) based on Nvidia’s DSX POD reference design that allows partners to preintegrate Nvidia Vera Rubin rack-scale AI infrastructure and complete critical validation before shipment.

The designs can reduce power consumption by about 30 percent and improve token output per watt by about 50 percent, Liu said, adding that achieving such gains requires close cooperation with Nvidia.

Separately, Hon Hai unveiled three new reference electric vehicles: the SUV-inspired Model A+ and Model K+, as well as the compact Model K pickup truck.

Hon Hai is in talks with automakers and other potential partners and would disclose further details once agreements are reached, Liu said.

The company would continue to follow its contract design and manufacturing service model, instead of establishing its own automotive brand, he said.

data.title: Central bank members show concern about inflation
data.description:
Central bank board members expressed concern about rising inflation, but differed on whether to raise interest rates, with two directors favoring a hike — including one who called for monetary policy normalization — while the majority supported holding rates steady, minutes of the bank’s meeting last month showed.

Directors said that import and producer prices were potential sources of further consumer inflation, while the government’s measures to stabilize energy prices had helped shield consumers from higher oil costs.

One director said that Taiwan should begin normalizing monetary policy, saying a rate increase would not necessarily be intended to curb inflation or slow economic activity, but to move borrowing costs toward a more neutral level after a prolonged period of exceptionally low rates.

Other directors favored keeping rates unchanged, saying that inflation in Taiwan is more moderate than in the US, the eurozone and South Korea, where price increases had exceeded 3 percent.

The central bank had tightened financial conditions without raising its benchmark rate since March 2024, using higher reserve requirements, stricter property lending rules and open-market operations, they said.

Keeping rates unchanged while the US Federal Reserve raised its policy rate could widen the interest-rate gap between the two economies, putting further downward pressure on the New Taiwan dollar and pushing up import costs, one director said.

The director cited rising producer prices for domestically produced goods sold locally and increases in import prices as threats to the consumer price outlook.

However, other directors said that higher rates could deepen disparities in access to credit.

Technology companies benefiting from strong artificial intelligence-related demand and profitability are generally less sensitive to borrowing costs than traditional manufacturers, they said.

With financing demand from the information and communications technology sector already contributing to tight liquidity, higher rates could make it more difficult for small and medium-sized enterprises, micro-businesses and traditional manufacturers to secure funding, they said.

Directors also highlighted the uneven recovery in domestic demand.

Despite surging exports, private consumption has remained comparatively subdued, limiting the extent to which rapid economic growth has translated into broader inflationary pressure.

Higher import prices for electronic components have also largely been reflected in export prices, while energy-price stabilization measures have helped contain the pass-through of oil costs to consumers.

Separately, one director urged the central bank to closely monitor banks’ growing lending to securities firms amid rapid stock trading, warning that a sharp market correction could expose lenders to greater risks.

All of the board members agreed that policy decisions should take into account inflation trends, domestic financial conditions and monetary policy moves by major overseas central banks.

data.title: Delta says Q4 revenue to rise from last quarter
data.description:
Delta Electronics Inc (台達電) on Thursday said that revenue this quarter would increase from the previous quarter’s NT$197.06 billion (US$6.07 billion), driven by rising demand for its power and thermal management products amid robust investment in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure.

Order momentum for this quarter remains high and is expected to extend into next year, supported by robust demand for AI data center-related products, Delta chairman Ping Cheng (鄭平) told an earnings conference.

Despite component shortages, power constraints, labor shortfalls and project delays, long-term AI data center demand and growth remain intact, Cheng said.

“I think no matter what [short-term] problems it faces, the trend remains unchanged,” Cheng said, adding that Delta remains optimistic about its long-term business outlook.

Data center and AI-related products accounted for about 50 percent of the company’s revenue of NT$539.7 billion in the first three quarters of this year, he said.

Capital expenditure among the world’s four major cloud service providers is expected to top US$1 trillion next year, driving global data center investment to US$1.5 trillion, Delta vice president Lanford Liu (劉亮甫) said.

Power electronics products accounted for 54 percent of Delta’s revenue last quarter, followed by infrastructure products at 33 percent, automation devices at 8 percent and mobility applications at 5 percent, the company said.

Delta reported net profit of NT$23.5 billion last quarter, down 6.5 percent quarter-on-quarter, but up 26.3 percent year-on-year.

The earnings results were the strongest for the third quarter in the company’s history.

Third-quarter earnings per share dropped to NT$9.04 from NT$9.68 the previous quarter, but were up from NT$7.16 a year earlier.

Gross margin fell to 34.08 percent last quarter from 35.64 percent the previous quarter and 34.87 percent a year earlier as component shortages and delays in customers’ data center construction plans pushed up inventory costs, Delta said.

Gross margin is expected to be no lower than last quarter, Cheng said.

Material costs have risen about 2 percent since the beginning of this year, Cheng said.

Delta is considering price hikes this quarter or next quarter due to higher material costs, he said.

Delta booked inventory write-down provisions equivalent to about 1.7 percent of revenue last quarter, mainly due to customer order adjustments, chief financial officer Yu Po-wen (余博文) said.

In its thermal solutions business, liquid-cooling products accounted for 13 percent of Delta’s revenue, or about NT$25 billion, last quarter and are expected to remain at a similar percentage for the rest of this year, Yu said.

Separately, Delta’s Singapore subsidiary on Wednesday approved a planned US$120 million capital injection into its wholly owned Malaysian subsidiary.

Delta plans to build a large production base in Malaysia and aims over about five years to expand its capacity to a scale comparable with its Thailand operations, Cheng said.

data.title: Q3 GDP growth hits 14.36%, highest in 48 years
data.description:
Taiwan’s economy grew by an estimated 14.36 percent in the third quarter from a year earlier, the highest growth for the quarter in 48 years, the Directorate-General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics (DGBAS) said yesterday.

The forecast was 2.94 percentage points higher than an August estimate.

It also marked the fourth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth.

DGBAS specialist Chiang Hsin-yi (江心怡) said stronger-than-expected exports and business investment were key drivers of the robust third-quarter growth.

On the export front, demand for artificial intelligence applications, high-performance computing and cloud services, as well as stronger orders for electronic components used in new consumer products, helped boost exports, Chiang said.

Higher prices for exported products also helped increase export value, she said.

Export demand also supported business investment, with real investment and changes in inventories estimated to have increased 26.36 percent in the third quarter, 4.26 percentage points higher than the previous forecast, she said.

Capital equipment imports, measured in New Taiwan dollars, rose 58.5 percent in the third quarter from a year earlier, including a 35.66 percent increase in semiconductor equipment, while investment in machinery, transportation equipment, intellectual property and construction also grew, the DGBAS said.

Meanwhile, exports from industries other than electronics and information and communications technology also grew at double-digit rates, indicating a gradual recovery in traditional industries in recent quarters, Chiang said.

On the domestic front, private consumption remained strong, helped by a recovery in the auto market and the wealth effect from Taiwan stocks reaching record highs, she said.

Real private consumption grew 5.37 percent in the third quarter, 0.01 percentage points above the August forecast.

It was the second consecutive quarter in which growth exceeded 5 percent, the DGBAS said.

The last time Taiwan recorded an extended period of double-digit growth was in 1986-1987, when the economy recorded high growth for six consecutive quarters as the government gradually eased capital controls and foreign exchange restrictions, contributing to economic liberalization and an economic upswing, Chiang said.

For the first three quarters, growth is estimated to have reached 14.22 percent, the highest for the period in half a century, the DGBAS said.

data.title: Citi launches new Client Center in Taiwan
data.description:
Reinforcing its commitment to the market and connecting clients to global opportunities, Citi today officially launched its new Client Center in Taiwan.

Inspired by three central themes, “Landscape,” “Seascape,” and “Culture,” the facility delivers a premium experience that reflects Taiwan’s distinctive character and Citi’s international perspective.

The Client Center provides an enhanced setting for engagement and collaboration, demonstrating Citi’s long-term investment in Taiwan, focus on building enduring relationships and support for the market’s continued development.

Over the years, Citi has stood alongside its clients through economic cycles and industry transformation, serving as a trusted bank as they grow and expand internationally.

The opening ceremony featured Edward Skyler, Citi’s Head of Enterprise Services and Public Affairs; Marc Luet, Citi’s Head of Japan, North Asia and Australia Cluster and Banking; and Christie Chang, Citi Country Officer for Taiwan and Chairperson of Citibank Taiwan Ltd.

Edward Skyler said: “We have been in Taiwan since 1964, and this new Client Center reflects the trust our clients have placed in us. It is an honor to help connect our Taiwanese clients to our global network, in Asia and increasingly beyond, and help them compete.”

Marc Luet added: “Taiwan is a strategically vital market for Citi, not only within Asia, but globally. As a highly advanced economy, a technology powerhouse, and a critical link in the global technology and manufacturing supply chain, Taiwan has been increasingly central to the global economy. The opening of our new Client Center marks an important milestone for Citi Taiwan and reaffirms our long-term commitment to supporting clients here, across Asia and around the world.”

Christie Chang said: “The opening of this Client Center represents more than the launch of a new space. It reflects Citi’s enduring commitment to serving clients in Taiwan and supporting their continued growth. The center embodies our client-first approach and our focus on creating value at every opportunity. With thoughtfully designed facilities and an elevated experience, it will provide a platform for closer engagement, meaningful dialogue and the development of innovative solutions.”

“This investment demonstrates the importance we place on helping businesses capture opportunities worldwide. Looking ahead, Citi will continue to draw on the strength of our global network, expertise, and capabilities to help turn our clients’ ambitions into results,” Chang said.

Taiwan is a key Asian economy with strong ties to international markets. Many of our clients operate, invest, manage supply chains and serve customers across multiple jurisdictions, creating a need for a financial partner that can connect them with cross-border resources, she said.

Citi’s new Client Center will serve as a strategic hub for dialogue and knowledge exchange, bringing global insights and opportunities to our Taiwan clients. By working together, we can help them remain connected to markets worldwide, anticipate emerging trends and position themselves for future growth, she said.

Citi also continues its long-standing investment in talent.

Christie Chang said: “The opening of our new Client Center marks an exciting chapter in Citi’s history in Taiwan. It demonstrates our ongoing focus on the local market, stronger relationships, and talent development. Exceptional talent is essential to delivering outstanding value, which is why we are committed to creating a workplace that encourages innovation, teamwork and excellence. Guided by our One Citi approach, we will bring together the full breadth of our network and capabilities to deliver comprehensive financial solutions and help businesses seize new possibilities.”

The new Client Center integrates local inspiration with Citi’s global outlook, creating a modern environment that combines aesthetics, cultural elements and functionality. The design is centered around three themes: Landscape Inspiration, Seascape Inspiration and Culture Inspiration.

The Client Center will serve as an important hub among Citi, its clients and business partners.

Through stronger connections and collaboration, Citi will help businesses explore opportunities, achieve milestones and navigate evolving trends with confidence. Its opening further highlights Citi’s presence in Taiwan and its dedication to supporting businesses as they expand beyond the market.

data.title: ASE raises capex budget to US$11.5bn
data.description:
ROOM TO GROW: The company’s biggest bottleneck is still space, chief financial officer Joseph Tung said, adding that it was scouting existing factories to acquire

ASE Technology Holding Co (日月光投控) yesterday raised its annual capital expenditure budget for the third time to US$11.5 billion, driven by expectations that customer demand next year would continue to outpace capacity, particularly for its leading-edge advanced packaging (LEAP) technologies used in artificial intelligence (AI) chips.

ASE, the world’s biggest chip packaging and testing service provider, plans to add US$1 billion to its US$10.5 billion outlay on capacity expansion.

About 60 percent of the US$500 million equipment budget would be allocated for LEAP and 40 percent for mainstream packaging technology capacity, ASE chief financial officer Joseph Tung (董宏思) told an online investors’ conference.

Next year’s capital outlay would escalate even further as the company grapples with persistent capacity crunches, he said, adding that ASE has 22 factory construction projects in Taiwan.

“Although demand is there, it is still difficult to catch up in terms of supply. For next year, we are expecting demand to be even higher than what we would be able to deliver,” Tung said. “I think the biggest bottleneck today is really still space.”

ASE is scouting manufacturing facilities to accelerate capacity expansion in addition to its greenfield projects, he said, in response to an analyst’s question about whether the company would consider acquiring idled factories to bump up capacity rapidly as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC, 台積電) has.

TSMC yesterday announced a NT$38.8 billion (US$1.2 billion) deal to acquire an AUO Corp (友達) flat-panel facility, clean room and associated plant equipment.

ASE yesterday also raised its annual LEAP revenue forecast to more than US$4 billion this year, from the US$3.7 billion estimate it gave three months earlier.

ASE’s new full-process service, a turnkey offering for advanced semiconductor packaging, is expected to contribute more than US$1 billion in revenue next year, more than tripling from US$300 million this year, the company said.

Additionally, it has broadened its offerings to include co-packaged optics services, which are expected to contribute more than US$500 million next year as part of the company’s LEAP revenue, Tung said.

Next year’s gross margin for ASE’s assembly, testing and materials (ATM) business is projected to rise each quarter, scaling up from a 30 percent baseline, driven by robust demand for its high-margin LEAP services, he said.

This quarter, consolidated revenue is expected to grow 6 percent to 8 percent sequentially, from NT$244.16 billion last quarter, he said.

Gross margin is expected to improve to 23 percent to 24 percent from 22.1 percent last quarter.

ATM revenue is expected to expand 11 percent to 13 percent sequentially this quarter, from NT$151.49 billion last quarter, Tung said, adding that gross margin for that business is to increase 1 to 2 percentage points from 30.6 percent last quarter.

ASE’s electronic manufacturing services business revenue is to hold steady on a quarterly basis, while that segment’s operating margin is expected to dip to about 2 percent this quarter from 3.3 percent in the previous quarter, he said.

The company yesterday reported its strongest quarterly net profit for 19 quarters, at NT$27 billion for last quarter, surging 28 percent sequentially from NT$21.07 billion. That was a 148 percent increase from NT$10.87 billion a year earlier.

Basic earnings per share rose to NT$6.13 from NT$4.8 in the second quarter and NT$2.50 in the third quarter last year.
